whyWrongByChoice.C: Fc receptors are on the splenic macrophages that engulf the platelets, not the antibody target on the platelet.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antibodies here bind surface membrane glycoproteins rather than inner-leaflet phospholipid.

questions.stem: A student is asked to name the process by which a cell becomes coated with antibodies, making it attractive to macrophages, as occurs with platelets in immune thrombocytopenia. Which of the following terms describes this process?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Agglutination

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chemotaxis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diapedesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Margination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Opsonization

explanation.summary: Coating a cell with antibodies is called opsonization, which makes the cell appetizing to macrophages.
explanation.whyCorrect: The process of coating cells with antibodies is called opsonization. Anything coated with antibodies, even the body's own platelets, looks particularly appealing to macrophages, which then phagocytose it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Agglutination is the clumping of cells together, not antibody coating that targets a cell for phagocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemotaxis is directed cell movement along a chemical gradient, not antibody coating.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Diapedesis is the passage of leukocytes through the vessel wall, unrelated to antibody coating.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Margination refers to leukocytes lining up along the vessel wall, a different process entirely.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman has immune thrombocytopenia. Antibodies bound to the surface of her platelets are characterized in the laboratory. Which of the following immunoglobulin classes is usually responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IgA

choices.label: B
choices.text: IgD

choices.label: C
choices.text: IgE

choices.label: D
choices.text: IgG

choices.label: E
choices.text: IgM

explanation.summary: The antiplatelet antibodies of ITP are usually IgG.
explanation.whyCorrect: In ITP, patients make antibodies, usually IgG, that bind to their own platelets. The Fc portion of this bound IgG is what splenic macrophages recognize through their Fc receptors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IgA is a mucosal antibody and is not the class described in ITP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IgD is largely a B-cell surface receptor and is not the mediator of platelet destruction here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgE mediates allergic and antiparasitic responses, not antiplatelet opsonization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IgM is the first antibody made in a primary response, but the antiplatelet antibodies in ITP are usually IgG.

questions.stem: A hematology fellow is preparing a talk on immune thrombocytopenia and wants to state how often the disease occurs in the United States. Which of the following best approximates its incidence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 case per 1,000,000 people

choices.label: B
choices.text: 5 to 10 cases per 1,000 people

choices.label: C
choices.text: 5 to 10 cases per 1,000,000 people

choices.label: D
choices.text: 5 to 10 cases per 100,000 people

choices.label: E
choices.text: 50 to 100 cases per 100,000 people

explanation.summary: ITP is fairly common, with an incidence of 5 to 10 cases per 100,000 people in the United States.
explanation.whyCorrect: Immune thrombocytopenia is fairly common, with an incidence of 5 to 10 cases per 100,000 people in the United States. That frequency is why it is a routine consideration in any patient with an isolated low platelet count.

whyWrongByChoice.A: One case per million would make ITP a rare disease, far less common than it actually is.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 5 to 10 per 1,000 would make ITP extraordinarily common, far above the reported incidence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 5 to 10 per million underestimates the incidence by a factor of about one hundred.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 50 to 100 per 100,000 overstates the incidence roughly tenfold.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man is evaluated for an isolated thrombocytopenia with no other blood count abnormality. A trainee says immune thrombocytopenia is unlikely because it is a disease of young women. Which of the following statements best addresses the trainee's reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More recent data show the incidence rises with advancing age

choices.label: B
choices.text: The disease has not been described in male patients

choices.label: C
choices.text: The disease occurs only in children after a viral illness

choices.label: D
choices.text: The disease occurs only with a known autoimmune condition

choices.label: E
choices.text: The incidence peaks in adolescence and declines thereafter

explanation.summary: ITP was historically viewed as a disease of young women, but more recent data show incidence increases with advancing age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Historically, immune thrombocytopenia has been considered a disease most common in young females, but more recent data show an increase with advancing age. An older man with an isolated thrombocytopenia can therefore have ITP.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ITP is not confined to women; the historical female predominance is a tendency, not an absolute.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A post-viral illness in children describes acute ITP, only one of the two presentations of the disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ITP is frequently primary or idiopathic, with no identified autoimmune condition at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The trend described is an increase with advancing age, not a peak in adolescence with later decline.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man is referred for a platelet count of 68,000/mm3 found on routine screening. He has no petechiae, no bruising, and no bleeding. The laboratory notes that his specimen was insufficiently anticoagulated. Which of the following best explains his low platelet count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hypersplenism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immune thrombocytopenia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Medication-related thrombocytopenia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pregnancy-related thrombocytopenia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pseudothrombocytopenia

explanation.summary: Pseudothrombocytopenia is a falsely low platelet count caused by a problem with the blood draw, such as an insufficiently anticoagulated specimen.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudothrombocytopenia is a falsely low platelet count resulting from problems in the blood draw, such as an insufficiently anticoagulated specimen. It is one of the conditions that must be excluded before diagnosing ITP, and the absence of any bleeding fits an artifactual result.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hypersplenism produces a genuinely low peripheral count from splenic trapping, and no splenomegaly is described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ITP is a diagnosis of exclusion and cannot be made while a specimen artifact explains the count.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No medication is implicated in this case, and a specimen problem is explicitly identified.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pregnancy-related thrombocytopenia is irrelevant in a male patient.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with chronic liver disease has a platelet count of 62,000/mm3. On examination his spleen is palpable well below the left costal margin. Which of the following best explains his low peripheral platelet count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A recently started medication is destroying his platelets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibodies from a recent virus cross-react with his platelets

choices.label: C
choices.text: The enlarged spleen is trapping circulating platelets

choices.label: D
choices.text: The marrow has stopped producing megakaryocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The specimen was drawn into an inadequately anticoagulated tube

explanation.summary: Hypersplenism makes the peripheral platelet count appear low because a big spleen traps platelets.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypersplenism is one of the conditions that must be excluded before ITP is diagnosed: a big spleen can trap platelets, making the peripheral count appear low. The palpable splenomegaly here points to trapping rather than antibody-mediated destruction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Medication-related thrombocytopenia is a separate exclusion, and no new drug is mentioned.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Molecular mimicry after a viral illness is a secondary cause of ITP, but no recent viral illness is described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Megakaryocyte production is not the problem described; splenic trapping explains a low peripheral count with intact production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A specimen problem describes pseudothrombocytopenia, and no drawing artifact is reported here.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation has a platelet count of 94,000/mm3 with a normal hemoglobin and white blood cell count. A repeat properly anticoagulated specimen confirms the count, she takes no medications, her spleen is not palpable, and she has had no recent infection. Which of the following must still be excluded before immune thrombocytopenia is diagnosed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypersplenism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Medication-related thrombocytopenia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pregnancy-related thrombocytopenia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pseudothrombocytopenia

explanation.summary: ITP is a diagnosis of exclusion, and pregnancy-related thrombocytopenia is on the list of conditions to rule out.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because there are no specific laboratory tests or diagnostic criteria for ITP, other causes of the thrombocytopenia must be ruled out. Pregnancy-related thrombocytopenia is explicitly one of those conditions, and in this patient it is the only listed exclusion not yet addressed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is a secondary cause of ITP, not an exclusion, and her white cell count is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypersplenism has already been addressed; her spleen is not palpable.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A medication effect is already excluded because she takes no medications.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudothrombocytopenia has been excluded by the confirmatory properly anticoagulated specimen.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has a platelet count of 41,000/mm3 with normal red and white cell counts. He started a new prescription drug 2 weeks ago, has had no recent viral illness, has no palpable spleen, and a repeat specimen confirms the count. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin prednisone for immune thrombocytopenia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform a bone marrow biopsy to confirm the diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review his medications for a drug-related cause

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schedule splenectomy to stop platelet destruction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfuse platelets to normalize his count

explanation.summary: Medication-related thrombocytopenia is one of the conditions that must be excluded before ITP is diagnosed.
explanation.whyCorrect: ITP is a diagnosis of exclusion, and medication-related thrombocytopenia is on the list of conditions to rule out. With a new drug started two weeks before the low count, reviewing the medications comes before committing to an ITP diagnosis and its treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Starting corticosteroids assumes an ITP diagnosis that has not yet been reached, since a drug cause remains unexcluded.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A bone marrow biopsy is not required to diagnose ITP and would not identify a drug cause.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splenectomy is a third-line therapy for refractory ITP, not a diagnostic step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Platelet transfusion is generally avoided and is reserved for severe thrombocytopenia with significant bleeding.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman with immune thrombocytopenia relapses as her prednisone is tapered, and rituximab is started. Which of the following best describes this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A cytotoxic chemotherapy agent given in cycles

choices.label: B
choices.text: A glucocorticoid used as first-line therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: A monoclonal antibody directed against CD20

choices.label: D
choices.text: A thrombopoietin receptor agonist taken orally

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pooled human immune globulin given intravenously

explanation.summary: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 antibody and is the typical first choice when ITP relapses after a steroid taper.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 antibody and is the typical first choice for relapse after a steroid taper. By targeting CD20-bearing B cells it addresses the source of the antiplatelet antibodies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rituximab is a targeted monoclonal antibody rather than cytotoxic chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The glucocorticoid used first line is prednisone, not rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The thrombopoietin agonists are eltrombopag and romiplostim, a different drug class from rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pooled intravenous immune globulin describes IVIG, which is given to raise the count rapidly.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with immune thrombocytopenia has a recurrence after her corticosteroid taper, and her hematologist elects to use a thrombopoietin agonist. Which of the following drugs is she most likely to receive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eltrombopag

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intravenous immune globulin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prednisone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rituximab

choices.label: E
choices.text: Warfarin

explanation.summary: Eltrombopag and romiplostim are the thrombopoietin agonists used for recurrence after a steroid taper.
explanation.whyCorrect: TPO agonists such as eltrombopag and romiplostim can be used for recurrence of ITP after a steroid taper. They are one of the options that displaced splenectomy from its former place in the treatment sequence.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IVIG is pooled immune globulin used to raise the count rapidly, not a TPO agonist.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prednisone is the corticosteroid she has already tapered, not a thrombopoietin agonist.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 antibody, a different class used for relapse after steroid taper.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Warfarin is an anticoagulant and has no role in treating a bleeding disorder such as ITP.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman with immune thrombocytopenia has failed corticosteroid therapy. Her physician notes that splenectomy once would have been the standard next step. Which of the following best describes the current role of splenectomy in ITP?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An effective third-line option after rituximab or TPO agonists

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contraindicated because the spleen is uninvolved in the disease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preferred over drug therapy because it works within hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reserved for children with acute post-viral disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: The usual first-line therapy for newly diagnosed disease

explanation.summary: Splenectomy was once standard for corticosteroid failure but is now a third-line option behind rituximab and TPO agonists.
explanation.whyCorrect: Splenectomy was previously the standard therapy for corticosteroid failure, but it has now been replaced by rituximab or TPO agonists. It remains effective and is used third line, and in refractory symptomatic disease it removes the source of platelet destruction.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The spleen is central to the disease, since splenic macrophages destroy the opsonized platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The treatment used to raise the count rapidly is IVIG; splenectomy is not chosen for speed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acute ITP in children is self-limited and generally requires no treatment at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: First-line therapy is corticosteroids such as prednisone, not surgery.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with chronic immune thrombocytopenia has a platelet count of 34,000/mm3 and no bleeding. She asks what her treatment is meant to accomplish. Which of the following best describes the goal of therapy in chronic ITP?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eliminate the antiplatelet antibodies from the circulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep the platelet count above 100,000/mm3 at all times

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prevent bleeding rather than normalize the platelet count

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restore the platelet count above 150,000/mm3 permanently

choices.label: E
choices.text: Titrate therapy to the tight correlation between count and bleeding

explanation.summary: In chronic ITP the aim is to keep the count at a safe level that prevents bleeding, not to make it normal.
explanation.whyCorrect: The goal of treatment is to keep the platelet count at a safe level to prevent severe bleeding. In chronic ITP specifically, the goal is to prevent bleeding, not to maintain a normal platelet count, and patients often tolerate a lower count without significant bleeding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Therapy is directed at safe platelet levels and bleeding prevention, not at clearing the antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No fixed count such as 100,000/mm3 is the goal, since bleeding risk tracks the count poorly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Returning the count to the normal range permanently is not the therapeutic target in chronic ITP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The correlation between platelet count and bleeding risk in ITP is actually poor, not tight.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman with newly diagnosed immune thrombocytopenia is told that the severity of the platelet reduction varies widely in this disease. Which of the following platelet counts represents the very minor end of that range?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Under 10,000/mm3

explanation.summary: Thrombocytopenia in ITP ranges from very minor (100,000-149,000/mm3) to very severe (under 10,000/mm3).
explanation.whyCorrect: The thrombocytopenia in ITP may range from very minor, for example 100,000-149,000/mm3, to very severe, for example under 10,000/mm3. A count of 100,000-149,000/mm3 is below the 150,000/mm3 threshold yet represents only a mild reduction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 10,000 to 49,000/mm3 is a substantial reduction, not the minor end of the range.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A count under 10,000/mm3 is the example given for very severe thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 150,000 to 249,000/mm3 falls within the normal platelet range, so it is not thrombocytopenia at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 250,000 to 400,000/mm3 is a normal count and would not be described as any degree of thrombocytopenia.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is brought to clinic with pinpoint petechiae over his legs that appeared suddenly three weeks after receiving the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine. He looks and feels well. His complete blood count shows a platelet count of 22,000/mm3 with a normal hemoglobin and white blood cell count. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aplastic anemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemophilia A

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immune thrombocytopenia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation.summary: Antiviral vaccines such as mumps, measles, and rubella are among the recognized secondary causes of ITP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Antiviral vaccines, for example mumps, measles, and rubella, are listed among the secondary causes of ITP. The abrupt petechial rash in a well-appearing child with an isolated thrombocytopenia is the classic picture of acute ITP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leukemia would be expected to disturb the white cell count and other lines rather than platelets alone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aplastic anemia depresses all cell lines, so the thrombocytopenia would not be isolated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemophilia A is an inherited factor deficiency with a normal platelet count, not an isolated thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Iron deficiency anemia would show an abnormal red cell picture; his hemoglobin is normal.

questions.stem: The parent of a teenager asks whether COVID-19 vaccination will cause immune thrombocytopenia. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cases are reported, but an increased incidence is not clear

choices.label: B
choices.text: The disease has never been reported after any vaccination

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vaccination causes the disease more often than viral infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vaccination is a proven common cause of the disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaccine-associated cases are permanent and untreatable

explanation.summary: Cases of ITP have been reported after COVID-19 vaccination, but it is not clear that vaccination actually increases the incidence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cases have been reported after COVID-19 vaccination, but it is not clear whether there is an actual increased incidence with vaccination. Reported association is not the same as an established rise in disease frequency.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cases following antiviral vaccines, including COVID-19 vaccination, have indeed been reported.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No such comparison is supported; viral illnesses are well-described triggers through molecular mimicry.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vaccination has not been established as a common cause; the link remains uncertain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nothing indicates that vaccine-associated cases behave differently or resist the usual treatments.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with recurrent fetal loss and a prior deep venous thrombosis is found to have antiphospholipid syndrome. She now presents with petechiae and an isolated thrombocytopenia. Which category of secondary cause of immune thrombocytopenia does her condition represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hematopoietic neoplasm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypersplenism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Medication effect

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viral illness acting through molecular mimicry

explanation.summary: Antiphospholipid syndrome, like lupus, is an autoimmune secondary cause of ITP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autoimmune diseases such as lupus and antiphospholipid syndrome are listed secondary causes of ITP. In these conditions normal immune processes have gone awry and antibodies are made against all sorts of self-antigens, including those on platelets.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The neoplastic secondary cause cited is chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypersplenism traps platelets in an enlarged spleen and is not an antibody-mediated cause.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Medication-related thrombocytopenia is a separate condition to exclude, and no drug is implicated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Molecular mimicry describes cross-reacting antibodies after a viral illness such as HIV or hepatitis C.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma develops an isolated thrombocytopenia attributed to secondary immune thrombocytopenia. His underlying malignancy is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A myeloproliferative neoplasm

choices.label: B
choices.text: A peripheral B-cell neoplasm

choices.label: C
choices.text: A peripheral T-cell neoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: A plasma cell dyscrasia

choices.label: E
choices.text: A variant of acute myeloid leukemia

explanation.summary: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma is one of the peripheral B-cell neoplasms and is a secondary cause of ITP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma is one of the peripheral B-cell neoplasms, and it is listed among the secondary causes of immune thrombocytopenia. Chronic ITP may be secondary to this hematopoietic neoplasm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Myeloproliferative neoplasms are of myeloid origin, whereas CLL/SLL is lymphoid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CLL/SLL arises from B cells, not T cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasma cell dyscrasias are a distinct group and are not the classification given for CLL/SLL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: It is a chronic lymphoid neoplasm rather than an acute myeloid leukemia.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman with chronic immune thrombocytopenia asks what the most dangerous, though rare, complication of her condition would be. Which of the following is the best answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A nosebleed lasting several minutes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Easy bruising of the thighs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Heavier than usual menstrual flow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intracerebral hemorrhage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Petechiae over the lower legs

explanation.summary: Life-threatening bleeding in ITP, such as intracerebral or uncontrollable gastrointestinal bleeding, is rare.
explanation.whyCorrect: In most cases of chronic ITP the bleeding is relatively minor. Life-threatening bleeding, such as intracerebral bleeding or uncontrollable gastrointestinal bleeding, is rare, particularly with appropriate treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nosebleeds are among the typical minor bleeding symptoms of chronic ITP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Easy bruising is one of the milder presenting symptoms of the disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Excessive menstrual flow is a common symptom of chronic ITP rather than a fatal complication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Petechiae are a common and relatively minor manifestation, not a life-threatening complication.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman has had gradually increasing petechiae, occasional nosebleeds, and easy bruising over several months and is diagnosed with chronic immune thrombocytopenia. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in her history?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A spleen palpable below the costal margin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diffuse lymphadenopathy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excessive menstrual flow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recurrent bleeding into the knee joints

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scleral icterus and dark urine

explanation.summary: Chronic ITP has a gradual onset with petechiae, nosebleeds, easy bruising, and excessive menstrual flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: The onset of chronic ITP is usually gradual, characterized by petechiae, nosebleeds, easy bruising, and excessive menstrual flow, with recurrences being common. Heavy menses fit that mucocutaneous bleeding pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Splenomegaly suggests hypersplenism, a condition to exclude; the spleen is typically not enlarged in ITP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diffuse lymphadenopathy points toward a lymphoproliferative disorder rather than ITP itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bleeding into joints is not part of the described presentation of ITP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Jaundice and dark urine suggest hemolysis, and in ITP the red cells are normal.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with mild systemic lupus erythematosus has scattered petechiae, heavier menses for 3 months, an isolated thrombocytopenia, and no other identifiable cause. She has no significant bleeding. In addition to monitoring her counts, which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arrange hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Begin weekly intravenous immune globulin indefinitely

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give prophylactic platelet transfusions every month

choices.label: D
choices.text: Proceed with splenectomy to stop platelet destruction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Refer her for treatment of the underlying autoimmune disease

explanation.summary: In secondary ITP, treating the underlying disorder, such as lupus, should resolve the thrombocytopenia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her isolated thrombocytopenia with a history of lupus and no other secondary cause indicates immune thrombocytopenia secondary to her lupus. Referral to a rheumatologist to consider treatment of the lupus should resolve the thrombocytopenia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stem cell transplantation has no role here; her marrow production of platelets is intact.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IVIG is used to raise the count rapidly in bleeding or pre-operative settings, and its effect is transient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Platelet transfusions are generally avoided because the transfused platelets are rapidly destroyed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splenectomy is a third-line option for refractory disease, not an initial step in mild secondary ITP.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with chronic immune thrombocytopenia has a platelet count of 112,000/mm3. She has no petechiae, no bruising, and no bleeding of any kind, and her red and white cell counts are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give intravenous immune globulin to raise the count

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observation with monitoring of her platelet count

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule splenectomy after appropriate immunization

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start prednisone to normalize her platelet count

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start rituximab to suppress antibody production

explanation.summary: Treatment in ITP is typically reserved for patients with severe bleeding or very low platelet counts.
explanation.whyCorrect: The goal of treatment is to keep the platelet count at a safe level to prevent severe bleeding, and treatment is typically given to patients with severe bleeding or with very low platelet counts. This patient has neither, and in chronic ITP the aim is to prevent bleeding rather than to maintain a normal count.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IVIG is used for significant bleeding or as pre-operative treatment, and its effect is transient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Splenectomy is a third-line option for refractory symptomatic disease, not for mild asymptomatic thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Corticosteroids are first-line therapy when treatment is indicated, but normalizing the count is not the goal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rituximab is reserved for relapse after a steroid taper, not for an untreated, asymptomatic patient.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man who underwent a bone marrow transplant 10 days ago has thrombocytopenia. His platelet count was 120,000/mm3 on Monday and 100,000/mm3 on Wednesday, and it continues to fall. Below which of the following platelet counts is he most likely to develop spontaneous bleeding?

explanation.summary: Spontaneous (non-traumatic) bleeding generally does not occur until the platelet count drops below 10,000/mm3.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's platelet count table shows that the risk of spontaneous bleeding appears only when counts fall below 10,000/mm3. Above that level, bleeding, if any, is usually provoked by trauma rather than occurring spontaneously.

whyWrongByChoice.B: At counts around 20,000-50,000/mm3 a patient may bleed more after injuries, but spontaneous bleeding is not expected.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A count of 60,000/mm3 is not usually associated with significant bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A count of 80,000/mm3 is above the threshold for any abnormal bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A count of 100,000/mm3 is only mild thrombocytopenia and is not associated with significant bleeding.

questions.stem: A sample of platelet-rich plasma is sent to the laboratory for aggregation studies. When exposed to ADP, collagen, epinephrine, and ristocetin, the platelets aggregate normally in response to every agent. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by these results?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The patient has abnormal platelet function

choices.label: B
choices.text: The patient has Bernard-Soulier syndrome

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patient is able to form a normal fibrin clot

choices.label: D
choices.text: The platelets are functioning normally

choices.label: E
choices.text: The sample contains a sufficient quantity of platelets

explanation.summary: Aggregation to all agonists indicates normal platelet function; the test does not assess platelet quantity or fibrin formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Normal platelets respond to every aggregating agent, so aggregation with ADP, collagen, epinephrine, and ristocetin is considered normal platelet function. Abnormal responses to one or more agents would instead suggest a functional defect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abnormal function would show diminished aggregation to one or more agents, which is not the case here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bernard-Soulier would show absent aggregation to ristocetin, so a normal ristocetin response excludes it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Platelet aggregation studies assess primary hemostasis and do not evaluate fibrin (secondary hemostasis).
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aggregation studies measure how platelets respond, not how many platelets are present.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman is referred after continuous oozing from wisdom-tooth extraction sites. Her prothrombin time/INR, partial thromboplastin time, and platelet count are all within normal limits. Which of the following tests is the preferred next step to evaluate how well her platelets function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hemoglobin electrophoresis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Peripheral blood smear for morphology

choices.label: C
choices.text: Platelet count

choices.label: D
choices.text: Platelet function assay (PFA-100)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prothrombin time

explanation.summary: The PFA-100 is the preferred test of platelet function, assessing how well the platelet plug forms.
explanation.whyCorrect: When counts and coagulation studies are normal but bleeding persists, a platelet function problem is suspected. The PFA-100 is the preferred assay of platelet function; blood is drawn through a standardized aperture and the machine measures plug formation, detecting abnormal adhesion and aggregation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemoglobin electrophoresis evaluates hemoglobin types and is unrelated to platelet function.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Morphology can reveal size/shape abnormalities but most diseases have normal-appearing platelets and it does not measure function.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The platelet count is already normal and does not indicate how well the platelets work.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The prothrombin time evaluates the coagulation cascade, not platelet function, and is already normal.

questions.stem: During a platelet aggregation study, a patient's platelets aggregate normally in response to ADP, collagen, and epinephrine but fail to aggregate in response to ristocetin. Genetic and receptor testing shows the platelets lack the normal glycoprotein Ib (GpIb) receptor for von Willebrand factor. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bernard-Soulier syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemophilia A (factor VIII)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura

choices.label: D
choices.text: Essential thrombocytosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding

explanation.summary: Bernard-Soulier syndrome is caused by a lack of the platelet GpIb receptor for vWF, producing absent ristocetin-induced aggregation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ristocetin works by driving vWF (GpIb) receptors to the platelet surface so they can bind vWF. In Bernard-Soulier syndrome the platelets lack the normal GpIb receptor, so no matter how much ristocetin is added the platelets will not aggregate, while responses to other agonists remain normal.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemophilia A is a factor VIII deficiency of secondary hemostasis and does not affect platelet aggregation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immune thrombocytopenia lowers the platelet count rather than removing the GpIb receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thrombocytosis is a high platelet count and does not cause an isolated loss of ristocetin response.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin K deficiency impairs the coagulation cascade, not platelet ristocetin aggregation.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with lifelong easy bruising and heavy menses undergoes aggregation testing. Her platelets aggregate normally to ADP, collagen, and epinephrine but fail to aggregate with ristocetin. Repeat testing after mixing her platelets with normal von Willebrand factor restores the ristocetin response. Which of the following best explains her original result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of GpIb, the platelet receptor for von Willebrand factor

choices.label: B
choices.text: An elevated platelet count causing sludging

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deficiency of coagulation factor VIII

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deficiency of von Willebrand factor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lack of platelet granules

explanation.summary: In von Willebrand disease the platelets are normal but there is no functional vWF, so ristocetin-induced aggregation is absent.
explanation.whyCorrect: In von Willebrand disease the platelets express normal vWF (GpIb) receptors, but there is no normal von Willebrand factor for them to bind, so they do not aggregate with ristocetin. Supplying normal vWF corrects the defect, distinguishing it from Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: If the GpIb receptor itself were absent (Bernard-Soulier), adding normal vWF would not restore aggregation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A high platelet count causes sludging/ischemia, not a selective loss of the ristocetin response.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Factor VIII deficiency affects the coagulation cascade, not ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Absent granules is a different morphologic defect and would not be corrected by adding vWF.

questions.stem: A hematology technician reports that an automated analyzer produced a platelet count that appears falsely low. Small clumps of platelets were noted when the specimen was checked. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to obtain an accurate platelet count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Manually examine a blood smear

choices.label: B
choices.text: Measure the von Willebrand factor level

choices.label: C
choices.text: Order a bleeding time

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform a platelet function assay (PFA-100)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Perform ristocetin aggregation testing

explanation.summary: When platelet clumps or other small cells cause a falsely altered automated count, the count should be verified manually on a smear.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although modern analyzers usually give reliable counts, platelet clumps or misread small cells can falsely elevate or decrease the automated result. In these instances the platelet count must be performed manually by examining a blood smear under the microscope.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A vWF assay measures von Willebrand factor level and does not quantify platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The bleeding time assesses function of primary hemostasis, not the platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The PFA-100 measures platelet function, not the number of platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ristocetin aggregation testing evaluates platelet response to vWF, not quantity.

questions.stem: A medical student asks why the platelet function assay (PFA-100) has largely replaced the older bleeding time test. Which of the following is the best explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bleeding time cannot be performed when the platelet count is normal

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bleeding time evaluates the coagulation cascade rather than platelets

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bleeding time is difficult to standardize

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bleeding time measures fibrin formation directly

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bleeding time requires platelet-rich plasma and aggregating agents

explanation.summary: The bleeding time is hard to standardize, which is why the PFA-100 is replacing it.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bleeding time involves piercing the forearm with a lancet and recording how long the cut bleeds. It is being replaced by the PFA-100 because it is difficult to standardize, with variables such as the size of the lancet, the skin depth and durability, and the technician's blotting technique.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The bleeding time evaluates function and can be done with a normal platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Both the bleeding time and PFA-100 assess platelet-driven primary hemostasis, not the coagulation cascade.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neither the bleeding time nor the PFA-100 reflects fibrin formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Platelet-rich plasma and aggregating agents describe aggregation studies, not the bleeding time.

questions.stem: A patient with abnormal bleeding has a PFA-100 result showing decreased platelet function and a bleeding time that is prolonged. The clinician notes that neither of these tests reveals the underlying cause of the platelet dysfunction. Which of the following tests would best help determine the specific cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mean platelet volume measurement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Platelet aggregation studies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prothrombin time with INR

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat bleeding time testing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat automated platelet count

explanation.summary: Neither the PFA-100 nor the bleeding time explains why platelets malfunction; aggregation studies with specific agents narrow the cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: The PFA-100 and bleeding time show that platelets are working poorly but not why. Determining the cause is done using platelet aggregation studies that show the response to specific factors, since the pattern of response to different agents helps narrow the diagnosis (for example, Bernard-Soulier or von Willebrand disease).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mean platelet volume reflects platelet size, which does not necessarily reflect function or its cause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The prothrombin time evaluates the coagulation cascade, not the cause of platelet dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Repeating the bleeding time would only reconfirm the functional defect without revealing its cause.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A platelet count gives quantity, not the cause of dysfunction, and is often normal in these patients.

questions.stem: A physician wants to assess how well a patient can form a clot before major elective surgery. Which of the following statements about the platelet count is most accurate in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A normal platelet count confirms that platelet adhesion and aggregation are normal

choices.label: B
choices.text: A normal platelet count does not indicate that the platelets function normally

choices.label: C
choices.text: A normal platelet count rules out von Willebrand disease as a cause of bleeding

choices.label: D
choices.text: The platelet count directly measures platelet aggregation in response to agonists

choices.label: E
choices.text: The platelet count evaluates the coagulation cascade as the PT and PTT do

explanation.summary: The platelet count reflects quantity, not function; a patient can bleed abnormally with a normal count.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick emphasizes that the platelet count does not indicate platelet function. A patient can have a bleeding disorder and still have a normal platelet count, which is why functional tests such as the PFA-100 and aggregation studies are needed to evaluate clotting ability.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A normal count does not confirm normal function; function requires separate testing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Von Willebrand disease can be present despite a normal platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aggregation is measured by aggregation studies, not by the platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The coagulation cascade is assessed by tests such as PT and PTT, not the platelet count.

questions.stem: A blood smear from a patient with a suspected hereditary platelet disorder shows unusually large platelets, and some platelets appear gray because they lack granules. Which of the following best describes the general clinical utility of assessing platelet morphology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can be reliably performed by automated analyzers alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: It directly measures the response of platelets to aggregating agents

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the initial step in evaluating any abnormal bleeding

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the preferred method to measure platelet function

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is used less often than the platelet count

explanation.summary: Morphology is used less frequently than the count because most diseases show normal-appearing platelets, though it is key in certain hereditary disorders.
explanation.whyCorrect: Assessing morphology requires manual smear review and is used less frequently than the total platelet count because most diseases, even those involving platelets, have normal-appearing platelets. In certain conditions, however, such as hereditary platelet disorders with giant platelets or gray platelets lacking granules, morphology is an important part of the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Morphology requires manual microscopic evaluation because autoanalyzers cannot detect subtle abnormalities.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Response to aggregating agents is measured by aggregation studies, not by morphology.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Measuring the platelet count, not morphology, is the initial step in evaluating abnormal bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The preferred measure of platelet function is the PFA-100, not morphology.

questions.stem: In a platelet aggregation study, an aggregating agent is added to a tube of platelet-rich plasma. As the reaction proceeds, the plasma becomes less cloudy (less turbid). Which of the following does this decrease in turbidity most directly indicate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fibrin is being formed in the tube by secondary hemostasis

choices.label: B
choices.text: The platelet count in the sample is falling as cells settle out

choices.label: C
choices.text: The platelets are aggregating in response to that agent

choices.label: D
choices.text: The platelets are failing to respond to that particular agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Von Willebrand factor is being consumed by the platelets

explanation.summary: In aggregation studies, platelets clumping together clears the plasma, so decreasing turbidity indicates aggregation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The principle of the test is that adding an aggregating agent to platelet-rich plasma causes platelets to clump together, which makes the plasma less cloudy or turbid. A decrease in turbidity therefore means the platelets are aggregating properly in response to that particular agent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aggregation studies assess platelet clumping, not fibrin formation (secondary hemostasis).
whyWrongByChoice.B: The clearing reflects platelets clumping, not a change in the total number of platelets present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A failure to respond would leave the plasma cloudy, not make it clearer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The turbidity change tracks platelet aggregation, not consumption of von Willebrand factor.

questions.stem: A patient with abnormal bleeding has normal aggregation to all agonists except ristocetin, to which the platelets do not respond. To distinguish von Willebrand disease from Bernard-Soulier syndrome, the clinician orders a von Willebrand factor assay (von Willebrand antigen). Which of the following results would best support a diagnosis of von Willebrand disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A low von Willebrand factor level

choices.label: B
choices.text: A normal von Willebrand factor level

choices.label: C
choices.text: An elevated platelet count

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreased mean platelet volume

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased fibrin formation

explanation.summary: The vWF assay measures the antigen level directly, and the level is low in von Willebrand disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both von Willebrand disease and Bernard-Soulier syndrome show absent ristocetin aggregation. A specialized von Willebrand factor assay (von Willebrand antigen) measures the vWF level directly, and this level will be low in von Willebrand disease, whereas in Bernard-Soulier the defect is the missing platelet receptor and vWF is present.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A normal vWF level would point away from von Willebrand disease and toward a platelet receptor defect such as Bernard-Soulier.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The platelet count is not the distinguishing feature between these two disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mean platelet volume reflects platelet size and does not establish a low vWF level.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fibrin formation is part of secondary hemostasis and is not measured by the vWF assay.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman has a complete blood count performed as part of a preparticipation sports physical. She has no history of easy bruising, epistaxis, or abnormal bleeding. Which of the following platelet counts would be within the normal reference range?

explanation.summary: A normal platelet count is 150,000 to 400,000 platelets/mm3 of blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: The platelet count is the lab test used to determine the number of platelets in the blood, and the normal value is 150,000 to 400,000 platelets/mm3. A count of 250,000/mm3 sits squarely inside that range, consistent with her lack of bleeding symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 90,000/mm3 lies below the lower limit of 150,000/mm3 and therefore represents thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 120,000/mm3 is also below 150,000/mm3 and qualifies as mild thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 430,000/mm3 exceeds the upper limit of 400,000/mm3 and represents thrombocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 600,000/mm3 is well above 400,000/mm3 and represents marked thrombocytosis.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man has a routine complete blood count showing a platelet count of 850,000/mm3. He has no bruising, petechiae, or mucosal bleeding. Which of the following complications is he at greatest risk of developing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent platelet aggregation in response to ristocetin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delayed clot maturation from impaired fibrin formation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ischemic events from sludgy, slowly flowing blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged oozing after minor cuts and injuries

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spontaneous bleeding from failure of platelet plug formation

explanation.summary: Thrombocytosis, a count above 400,000/mm3, can cause ischemic events because the blood becomes sludgy and flows slowly.
explanation.whyCorrect: A platelet count above 400,000/mm3 defines thrombocytosis. Patients with extremely high numbers of platelets may experience ischemic events, because the blood gets sludgy and flows slowly when so many platelets are present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Loss of ristocetin-induced aggregation reflects a receptor or von Willebrand factor defect, not thrombocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fibrin formation is carried out by the coagulation cascade and is not altered by a high platelet number.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased bleeding after injuries is associated with counts in the 20,000 to 50,000/mm3 range.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spontaneous bleeding appears when the count falls below 10,000/mm3, the opposite of his result.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy has a platelet count of 35,000/mm3. She has no bleeding at rest, and her oncologist counsels her about contact sports and other activity restrictions. Which of the following is the most likely clinical consequence at this platelet count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete absence of any bleeding abnormality

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of fibrin formation during clot maturation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased bleeding following injuries

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ischemic events from sludgy, slowly flowing blood

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spontaneous bleeding in the absence of trauma

explanation.summary: Counts of 20,000 to 50,000/mm3 may lead to increased bleeding after injuries.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her count falls in the 20,000 to 50,000/mm3 band, where patients may bleed more than expected after injuries. Abnormal bleeding begins to be seen once the count drops below 50,000/mm3, which is why activity restrictions are discussed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Some abnormal bleeding may start to appear below 50,000/mm3, so hemostasis is not entirely normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fibrin formation is a function of the coagulation cascade and is unaffected by the platelet number.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ischemic events from sludgy blood occur with thrombocytosis above 400,000/mm3.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spontaneous bleeding is a risk only once the count falls below 10,000/mm3.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man has a platelet count of 135,000/mm3 discovered incidentally on a complete blood count drawn before a routine dental cleaning. He has never had abnormal bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He has a functional platelet defect requiring aggregation studies

choices.label: B
choices.text: He has mild thrombocytopenia and is unlikely to bleed significantly

choices.label: C
choices.text: He has thrombocytosis and is at risk of ischemic events

choices.label: D
choices.text: He is at risk of spontaneous bleeding during the procedure

choices.label: E
choices.text: His platelet count falls within the normal reference range

explanation.summary: A count below 150,000/mm3 is thrombocytopenia, but mild thrombocytopenia usually causes no significant bleeding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thrombocytopenia is defined as a platelet count below 150,000/mm3, so 135,000/mm3 qualifies. Mild thrombocytopenia is usually accompanied by no significant bleeding, with abnormal bleeding appearing only once the count falls below 50,000/mm3.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nothing in his history or this result suggests a functional defect, and the count alone does not indicate one.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thrombocytosis requires a count above 400,000/mm3, far higher than his value.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spontaneous bleeding is a concern below 10,000/mm3, not at 135,000/mm3.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The normal range begins at 150,000/mm3, so his count is slightly below normal.

questions.stem: A patient with unexplained bleeding undergoes evaluation of clot formation. Testing demonstrates that the platelet plug forms normally, but fibrin is not generated by the coagulation cascade. This defect is best classified as an abnormality of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Platelet adhesion to the vessel wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Platelet aggregation into a growing plug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Platelet morphology and granulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primary hemostasis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Secondary hemostasis

explanation.summary: Platelet plug formation is primary hemostasis; fibrin formation by the coagulation cascade is secondary hemostasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Making a blood clot requires two things: forming a platelet plug and sealing that plug up with fibrin. Platelet plug formation is called primary hemostasis, and fibrin formation, which occurs by means of the coagulation cascade, is called secondary hemostasis. A failure of fibrin generation is therefore a defect of secondary hemostasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adhesion is a platelet step within primary hemostasis and is intact here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aggregation likewise contributes to the platelet plug, which is forming normally.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Morphology describes platelet size, shape, and granulation and has no bearing on fibrin generation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary hemostasis is platelet plug formation, which is explicitly normal in this patient.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man is undergoing evaluation for newly diagnosed leukemia. He has had no bleeding or bruising, yet the hematologist includes a platelet count in the initial workup. Which of the following best explains this decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A deficiency of one blood cell type often accompanies a deficiency of another

choices.label: B
choices.text: The platelet count detects abnormal platelet size and granulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: The platelet count identifies the specific cause of platelet dysfunction

choices.label: D
choices.text: The platelet count measures the activity of the coagulation cascade

choices.label: E
choices.text: The platelet count reflects how well platelets respond to agonists

explanation.summary: The platelet count belongs in the evaluation of any hematology disorder because cytopenias tend to occur together.
explanation.whyCorrect: The platelet count is used to evaluate patients with coagulation disorders, but it is also used during the evaluation of any type of hematology disorder, such as leukemias and anemias, because a deficiency of one cell type is often accompanied by a deficiency of another.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Size and granulation are judged by manual review of platelet morphology on a blood smear.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The specific cause of platelet dysfunction is pursued with aggregation studies and specialized tests, not the count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The coagulation cascade is assessed by tests such as the prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Responses to agonists are measured by platelet aggregation studies.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman begins a drug therapy that requires serial complete blood counts, and her physician follows the platelet count at each visit. Which of the following is the best reason for this monitoring?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To assess the size and granulation of her platelets

choices.label: B
choices.text: To detect adverse reactions to the therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: To determine whether her platelets aggregate normally

choices.label: D
choices.text: To evaluate the integrity of her coagulation cascade

choices.label: E
choices.text: To measure her circulating von Willebrand factor level

explanation.summary: Monitoring the platelet count during drug therapy helps avoid adverse reactions and follow progress in certain cancer treatments.
explanation.whyCorrect: It is helpful to monitor the platelet count in drug therapies to avoid adverse reactions, and to monitor progress in certain cancer treatments. A falling count can signal a drug effect before any bleeding appears.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Size and granulation require manual assessment of platelet morphology on a blood smear.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aggregation is measured by platelet aggregation studies using specific aggregating agents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The platelet count gives no information about the coagulation cascade.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The von Willebrand factor level requires a specialized vWF assay.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man is evaluated for recurrent nosebleeds and easy bruising. No laboratory studies have yet been obtained. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial test in determining the cause of his abnormal bleeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flow cytometry for platelet glycoprotein complexes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Platelet aggregation studies

choices.label: C
choices.text: Platelet count

choices.label: D
choices.text: Platelet function assay (PFA-100)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Von Willebrand antigen assay

explanation.summary: Measuring the platelet count is an initial step in determining the cause of abnormal bleeding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Measuring the platelet count is an initial step in determining the cause of abnormal bleeding, because it establishes whether the problem is one of platelet quantity before any functional testing is pursued.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Flow cytometry for glycoprotein complexes is a specialized study, not an initial screen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aggregation studies are used later, to determine why platelets already shown to function poorly are malfunctioning.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The PFA-100 is the preferred test of function, but it follows a count that shows adequate platelet numbers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vWF assay is a specialized test used to narrow the cause after aggregation studies.

questions.stem: An automated hematology analyzer reports an unexpectedly high platelet count in a patient who has no clinical findings of thrombocytosis. Inspection of the specimen shows numerous small cells in addition to platelets. Which of the following best explains the elevated result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Giant platelets were excluded from the automated tally

choices.label: B
choices.text: Other cells in the specimen were misread by the analyzer as platelets

choices.label: C
choices.text: The analyzer cannot report counts above 400,000/mm3

choices.label: D
choices.text: The patient has an unrecognized underlying thrombocytosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: The plasma was too turbid for the analyzer's optical detector

explanation.summary: Automated platelet counts can be falsely elevated when other small cells are misread as platelets.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hematology analyzers usually provide reliable counts, but platelet counts can be falsely elevated or decreased when other small cells are misread as platelets or when platelet clumps are present. The numerous small cells in this specimen explain the spuriously high value, and the count should be repeated manually on a smear.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leaving platelets out of the tally would lower, not raise, the reported count.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Analyzers report values well above 400,000/mm3; that number is simply the upper limit of normal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The absence of clinical findings plus interfering small cells points to a spurious result rather than true thrombocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Turbidity of plasma is the readout of aggregation studies, not a source of counting error.

questions.stem: A pathologist reviews a peripheral blood smear under the microscope specifically to assess platelet morphology. Which of the following features does this analysis evaluate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The number of platelets per cubic millimeter of blood

choices.label: B
choices.text: The plasma concentration of von Willebrand factor

choices.label: C
choices.text: The response of platelets to ristocetin and adenosine diphosphate

choices.label: D
choices.text: The size, shape, and granulation of the platelets

choices.label: E
choices.text: The time required for a standardized skin incision to stop bleeding

explanation.summary: Morphologic analysis looks at the physiological and pathological features of platelets, including size, shape, and granulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Assessment of platelet morphology requires manual evaluation of a blood smear under a microscope, which can reveal subtle morphologic abnormalities that autoanalyzer devices cannot detect. Such an analysis includes the physiological and pathological features of the platelets, including size, shape, and granulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Counting platelets is the platelet count, a separate test from morphologic review.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The vWF concentration is measured by a specialized von Willebrand factor assay.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Responses to ristocetin and ADP are measured in platelet aggregation studies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Timing a standardized skin incision describes the bleeding time.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman has a disease that directly involves the platelets, and her peripheral smear is reviewed as part of the evaluation. Which of the following platelet appearances is most likely to be seen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Normal-appearing platelets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Platelets fixed in large clumps

choices.label: C
choices.text: Platelets that lack granules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uniformly giant platelets

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uniformly small platelets

explanation.summary: Most diseases, even those that directly involve platelets, show normal-appearing platelets on the smear.
explanation.whyCorrect: Morphology analysis is used less frequently than the total platelet count because most diseases, even those that directly involve platelets, have normal-appearing platelets. A normal smear therefore does not exclude platelet disease, which is why functional testing is often still required.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clumping is a specimen phenomenon that interferes with automated counting rather than a disease morphology.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Granule-poor, gray platelets are likewise a feature of certain hereditary platelet disorders rather than of most diseases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Giant platelets are an uncommon finding largely limited to certain hereditary platelet disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Abnormally small platelets suggest a specific disease and are not the usual finding.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy has had easy bruising and prolonged bleeding from minor cuts since early childhood, and two maternal relatives are similarly affected. Which of the following smear findings would most strongly support a hereditary platelet disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A platelet count of 380,000/mm3

choices.label: B
choices.text: Platelets of normal size, shape, and granulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Platelets that aggregate normally with ristocetin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Platelets that clump together within the collection tube

choices.label: E
choices.text: Platelets that lack granules and appear gray

explanation.summary: Hereditary platelet disorders may show giant platelets or platelets that lack granules and appear gray.
explanation.whyCorrect: In certain diseases, morphology is a key part of the diagnosis. Hereditary platelet disorders, for example, may have giant platelets or platelets that lack granules and appear gray, so an agranular, gray population on the smear supports that category of disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 380,000/mm3 is within the normal reference range and says nothing about a hereditary defect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Normal morphology is what most diseases show and would not point to a hereditary disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A normal ristocetin response argues against, rather than for, a receptor-based platelet defect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Platelet clumping is a specimen phenomenon that falsely alters automated counting.

questions.stem: A laboratory runs a platelet function assay (PFA-100) on a patient's blood sample. The blood is fed into a machine containing specific chemicals that provoke the platelets. Which of the following does the instrument measure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How well a platelet plug forms over a standardized aperture

choices.label: B
choices.text: The fall in turbidity of platelet-rich plasma after an agonist

choices.label: C
choices.text: The number of platelets present per cubic millimeter of blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: The quantity of fibrin generated by the coagulation cascade

choices.label: E
choices.text: The time a lancet wound on the forearm takes to stop bleeding

explanation.summary: In the PFA-100, blood is fed into a machine with chemicals that cause platelets to form a plug over a standardized aperture.
explanation.whyCorrect: The PFA-100 is the preferred test used to determine platelet function. Blood is fed into a machine with specific chemicals that cause platelets to form a plug over a standardized aperture, and the test measures how well that platelet plug forms, detecting both abnormal platelet adhesion and aggregation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A fall in turbidity of platelet-rich plasma is the readout of platelet aggregation studies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Platelet quantity is reported by the platelet count, not by a functional assay.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The PFA-100 assesses primary hemostasis and does not reflect fibrin activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Timing a lancet wound on the forearm describes the bleeding time, the older test it is replacing.

questions.stem: A hematology laboratory is phasing out the bleeding time in favor of the platelet function assay (PFA-100). Which of the following best describes how these two measurements of platelet function differ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The PFA-100 assesses secondary hemostasis, whereas the bleeding time assesses primary hemostasis

choices.label: B
choices.text: The PFA-100 identifies the cause of platelet dysfunction, whereas the bleeding time does not

choices.label: C
choices.text: The PFA-100 is performed in vitro, whereas the bleeding time is performed in vivo

choices.label: D
choices.text: The PFA-100 reports platelet quantity, whereas the bleeding time reports platelet function

choices.label: E
choices.text: The PFA-100 requires platelet-rich plasma, whereas the bleeding time requires whole blood

explanation.summary: The PFA-100 is an in vitro assay that has supplanted the in vivo bleeding time as the first measurement of platelet function.
explanation.whyCorrect: The PFA-100 is an in vitro assay of platelet function, run by feeding a blood sample into an instrument, and it has supplanted the in vivo bleeding time, which is performed by lancing the patient's forearm and timing how long the cut bleeds. Both estimate primary hemostasis, so the difference lies in where the test is performed and how reproducibly it can be standardized.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both tests evaluate primary hemostasis; neither reflects fibrin activity or secondary hemostasis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neither test explains why the platelets are performing poorly, which is why aggregation studies are added.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neither test reports platelet quantity; both are measures of function.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Platelet-rich plasma is the specimen used in aggregation studies, not in the PFA-100.

questions.stem: A provider performs a bleeding time by piercing the skin of the forearm with a small lancet, blotting the site as a clot forms, and recording the time until the cut stops bleeding. Which of the following is the usual reference range for this test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2 to 9 minutes

choices.label: B
choices.text: 12 to 20 minutes

choices.label: C
choices.text: 15 to 60 seconds

choices.label: D
choices.text: 20 to 30 minutes

choices.label: E
choices.text: 45 to 60 minutes

explanation.summary: The reference range for the bleeding time is usually 2 to 9 minutes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bleeding time records how long a standardized lancet wound on the forearm bleeds, which represents the time it takes a person to perform primary hemostasis and form the platelet plug. The reference range for bleeding time is usually 2 to 9 minutes.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 12 to 20 minutes exceeds the upper limit of the reference range and would be a prolonged result.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 15 to 60 seconds is shorter than the time normally required to complete primary hemostasis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 20 to 30 minutes represents markedly prolonged bleeding, not a normal value.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 45 to 60 minutes far exceeds any normal bleeding time.

questions.stem: A patient being evaluated for abnormal bleeding has a normal platelet function assay (PFA-100) and a normal bleeding time. Which of the following aspects of clot formation remains unevaluated by these two tests?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adhesion of platelets to the injured subendothelial surface

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aggregation of platelets into a growing hemostatic plug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Formation of the initial platelet plug at the site of injury

choices.label: D
choices.text: The activity of fibrin and formation of a mature clot

choices.label: E
choices.text: The overall adequacy of primary hemostasis at the vessel wall

explanation.summary: Neither the PFA-100 nor the bleeding time reflects the activity of fibrin or the formation of a mature clot.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both the PFA-100 and the bleeding time measure how well primary hemostasis proceeds, meaning how well the platelet plug forms. Neither test reflects the activity of fibrin and the formation of a mature clot, so normal results do not exclude a defect in secondary hemostasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The PFA-100 detects abnormal platelet adhesion, so adhesion is covered by these tests.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The PFA-100 also detects abnormal platelet aggregation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plug formation is exactly what both tests are designed to measure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary hemostasis as a whole is what these two tests assess.

questions.stem: Ristocetin is added to a tube of platelet-rich plasma during a platelet aggregation study. Which of the following describes the direct action of ristocetin on the platelets?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It activates platelets by binding the P2Y12 receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: It causes platelets to move more glycoprotein Ib receptors to their surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: It cross-links adjacent platelets by bridging GPIIb/IIIa with fibrinogen

choices.label: D
choices.text: It exposes subendothelial collagen to the circulating platelets

choices.label: E
choices.text: It raises the plasma concentration of von Willebrand factor

explanation.summary: Ristocetin works by driving more vWF (GpIb) receptors to the platelet surface, a step required for binding vWF.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ristocetin works by causing platelets to move more vWF receptors, also called glycoprotein Ib (GpIb) receptors, to the platelet surface. That step is required for potential binding to vWF, which leads to platelet activation and aggregation, so the response depends on both the receptor and vWF being present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The P2Y12 receptor is the target of adenosine diphosphate, a different aggregating agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibrinogen bridging of GPIIb/IIIa complexes links platelets to one another but is not the action of ristocetin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Collagen is a separate aggregating agent; ristocetin does not expose subendothelium in a test tube.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ristocetin acts on the platelet receptors and does not add or increase von Willebrand factor.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry of a patient's platelets shows absence of a membrane glycoprotein complex. The platelets adhere normally to von Willebrand factor in the subendothelium, but they cannot bind fibrinogen and therefore fail to link to one another. Which of the following is most likely deficient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collagen

choices.label: B
choices.text: GpIb

choices.label: C
choices.text: GPIIb/IIIa

choices.label: D
choices.text: P2Y12

choices.label: E
choices.text: Von Willebrand factor

explanation.summary: Fibrinogen links platelets to one another by bridging the GPIIb/IIIa complexes of adjacent platelets.
explanation.whyCorrect: Platelet-to-platelet linkage occurs when fibrinogen bridges the GPIIb/IIIa complexes on adjacent platelets, whereas adhesion to the vessel wall occurs through GpIb binding vWF that is anchored to collagen. Normal adhesion with failed fibrinogen binding therefore localizes the defect to GPIIb/IIIa, one of the Gp complexes flow cytometry can quantify.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Collagen is a subendothelial matrix protein to which vWF anchors, not a platelet membrane complex.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GpIb is the vWF receptor used for adhesion, and adhesion is intact in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: P2Y12 is the platelet receptor for adenosine diphosphate and does not bind fibrinogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Von Willebrand factor is a plasma and subendothelial protein rather than a platelet membrane complex, and binding to it is normal.

questions.stem: Several aggregating agents are added to platelet-rich plasma during platelet aggregation studies. Which of the following agents produces platelet activation by acting at the platelet P2Y12 receptor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenosine diphosphate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Subendothelial collagen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epinephrine (alpha-2)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fibrinogen at GPIIb/IIIa

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ristocetin via GpIb

explanation.summary: Adenosine diphosphate activates platelets through the P2Y12 receptor.
explanation.whyCorrect: The aggregating agents used in these studies include ristocetin, collagen, adenosine diphosphate (ADP), and epinephrine. ADP is the agent that signals through the platelet P2Y12 receptor shown on the platelet surface alongside GpIb and GPIIb/IIIa.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Collagen is the subendothelial protein to which vWF anchors and is not a P2Y12 ligand.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epinephrine is one of the aggregating agents used in these studies but does not act at P2Y12.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibrinogen bridges GPIIb/IIIa complexes and is not one of the aggregating agents added in this test.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ristocetin acts by driving vWF (GpIb) receptors to the platelet surface.

questions.stem: A laboratory performs platelet aggregation studies on a patient with abnormal bleeding, repeating the test with several agents to establish the pattern of response. Which of the following sets of agents is used for this purpose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenosine diphosphate, epinephrine, fibrin, and factor VIII

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collagen, calcium, vitamin K, and plasmin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ristocetin, collagen, adenosine diphosphate, and epinephrine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ristocetin, fibrinogen, thrombin, and heparin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ristocetin, von Willebrand factor, GpIb, and GPIIb/IIIa

explanation.summary: Aggregation studies are repeated with ristocetin, collagen, adenosine diphosphate, and epinephrine.
explanation.whyCorrect: The test is repeated with several different aggregating agents, such as ristocetin, collagen, adenosine diphosphate (ADP), and epinephrine. Normal platelets respond to every agent, and failure to respond to one or more of them defines the pattern used to narrow the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fibrin and factor VIII are elements of secondary hemostasis and are not added as aggregating agents.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Calcium, vitamin K, and plasmin belong to coagulation and clot breakdown, not to the aggregation panel.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibrinogen, thrombin, and heparin act within the coagulation cascade rather than serving as the aggregating agents in this panel.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Von Willebrand factor, GpIb, and GPIIb/IIIa are the targets involved in adhesion and aggregation, not the reagents added to the tube.

questions.stem: Rather than testing a patient's platelets with a single aggregating agent, the laboratory repeats the study with several different agents. Which of the following best explains why multiple agents are used?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single agent cannot produce a measurable change in turbidity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each agent measures the activity of a different coagulation factor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal platelets respond to only one of the available agents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat testing corrects for platelet clumping in the specimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pattern of response across the agents helps narrow the diagnosis
